name: LM358 Dual Op-Amp
summary: The default jellybean op-amp: two channels, runs from a single supply, and cannot reach either rail.
notes: Not rail to rail. The output gets within about 1.5 V of V+ and the input common mode range stops 1.5 V below it too. On a 3.3 V rail that leaves almost nothing, which is why it misbehaves in modern designs.

The output does reach close to ground, which is the trick that makes single supply work at all. Sinking current near 0 V is weak though, about 30 uA typical and 12 uA guaranteed, without a pull-down resistor.
There is crossover distortion in the output stage. Fine for DC and sensor conditioning, audibly bad for audio. Use a TL072 or an NE5532 there.
0.7 MHz gain bandwidth, or 1.2 MHz on the LM358B. At a gain of 100 you have 7 kHz of bandwidth left, and no more.
The LM393 comparator shares this package and pin arrangement but has an open collector output. The two look identical on a board and are not interchangeable.
Pin 4 is the negative supply, which is ground in a single supply circuit. Pin 8 is V+. That is the opposite corner pair from most DIP-8 logic.

pins.name: V-
pins.note: Ground in a single supply circuit.

pins.name: V+
pins.note: 100 nF to ground at the pin.

circuit.title: Single-supply follower

parts.why: Output straight back to the inverting input. Unity gain, the simplest useful configuration.
Half-rail bias. On a single supply the input has to sit somewhere the amplifier can actually reach.
The lower half of the same divider.
Stops supply noise riding straight through the bias divider into the input.

circuit.note: The input range includes ground but the output does not: it only swings down to about 20 mV above the negative rail, and up to about 1.5 V below the positive one. The LM358 is not rail to rail, whatever the breakout board says.
